Early one morning in April 1883, I woke up to find Sherlock Holmes standing by my bed, fully dressed. <break time="0.8s" /> A young lady has come to see us in a great hurry, and I thought you would want to hear her story from the beginning. <break time="0.8s" /> The lady was dressed in black and wore a heavy veil, and she was shaking like a frightened animal. <break time="0.8s" /> It is not the cold that makes me shake, Mister Holmes, she said in a low voice, It is fear. <break time="0.8s" /> When she lifted her veil, we saw that her face was pale and her hair was already touched with gray, though she was still young. <break time="0.8s" /> Her name was Helen Stoner, and she lived with her stepfather, Doctor Grimesby Roylott, in an old house at Stoke Moran. <break time="0.8s" /> Doctor Roylott was the last member of a family that had once been very rich, but it had lost almost everything long ago. <break time="0.8s" /> He had worked as a doctor in India, where his terrible temper had once caused the death of a servant and sent him to prison. <break time="0.8s" /> After Helens mother died in a railway accident, her money went to Doctor Roylott as long as her daughters lived with him. <break time="0.8s" /> Now he had no friends at all except the wandering gypsies, and he kept a cheetah and a baboon that ran freely around his land.

Two years ago, my twin sister Julia became engaged, and she was going to be married in just two weeks, Helen began. <break time="0.8s" /> Our three bedrooms were side by side on the ground floor, with the doctors room first, Julias in the middle, and mine at the end. <break time="0.8s" /> One night Julia asked me whether I had ever heard a low, clear whistle in the middle of the night, at about three oclock. <break time="0.8s" /> I had not, and we both thought that the sound might come from the gypsies who were camping on the land. <break time="0.8s" /> On that very night, during a wild storm, I heard a terrible scream, and I rushed out into the hall. <break time="0.8s" /> I heard a low whistle and then a loud clanging sound, as if a heavy piece of metal had fallen. <break time="0.8s" /> My sisters door opened, and she came out with her face white with terror, and then she fell to the floor. <break time="0.8s" /> She cried, Oh, my God, Helen, It was the band, The speckled band, and pointed toward the doctors room before she died. <break time="0.8s" /> The police found no marks on her body, and both her door and her window shutters had been locked from the inside. <break time="0.8s" /> Now I am engaged too, and I have had to move into Julias room, where last night I heard that same whistle.
